attribution_audit.composition: AUBREY I NEED YOU ON THIS SONG

findings.title: Existing publishing claims are a substantial part of this catalog.
findings.body: SUNDAE SONGS BANANA SPLIT explicitly names your writer identity in claims on works including “SYRUP DAMAGE” S659X5, “FIX AH FIEN” FC0FXK and “BIRD BATH” BE1JPQ. Those works each show 100% total known shares across listed interests. Across the reviewed catalog, 71 composition groups have a positive publisher/admin claim whose own writer chain names your identity. Confirm the applicable administration agreement, catalog scope and account statements before proposing additional administration. Registry claims do not establish actual payment.

findings.title: Separate apparent attribution gaps from claims needing chain verification.
findings.body: Your writer-name variants are evidenced on 108 unique composition groups, spanning 114 reviewed recordings. Of these, 12 have no attributable publishing/admin claim identified and merit split and representation investigation. A further 25 have an existing artist-associated publisher but no disclosed work-specific writer chain; those are held for verification and excluded from the apparent-gap count. The full-name writer identity often carries IPI 00721522675; plain TYREE THOMAS entries also carry other IPIs or no IPI. Verify the primary account and identity variants before filing or merging anything.

findings.title: High-exposure recordings already have work registrations.
findings.body: The ten sampled Spotify recordings total 91,968,511 plays; this is not a full-catalog total. “Kentucky Love” alone shows 34,489,796 plays and maps to KB5WEM, with 66.67% total known shares. Sundae has a 50% claim on that work, but its writer chain is empty in the returned record, so verify the chain rather than infer your personal split. “FREE JOE EXOTIC” FE9P1E and “FLINT FLOW” FJ0M6R each show 100% total known shares and artist-associated claims. Full-work coverage and your own attribution remain separate checks.

findings.title: Investigate existing works before creating new registrations.
findings.body: “OZEMPIC” OV545P shows 50% total known shares, “MORETHANBRILLIANT!” MI2B6Z 25%, and “CRAB RANGOON” CZ2ZES 30%. Each names your writer identity, but the reviewed recording link was not confirmed. The visible claims name co-writers Mathias Tuitasi, Remy Jones and Eric David Terrell respectively; none of those claims establishes an endpoint attributable to your interest. Obtain the relevant agreements, verify composition/version identity and investigate attaching the recordings to the existing works. The open remainders do not establish your entitlement.

findings.title: Crybaby needs a coordinated MLC/GMR reconciliation.
findings.body: The same “Crybaby” recording, QT6632601306, appears on two MLC works: C59CAL shows 60% total known shares and a Sundae claim naming TYREE JAWAN THOMAS; C57B9Z shows 25%, with Kevin Gates Music and Artist Publishing Global → Kobalt claims naming Kevin Gilyard. The writer identities differ between the two records. GMR also lists CRYBABY, work 100209913, naming TYREE JAWAN THOMAS, Kevin Gates and Flaw Da God, with 25% represented by GMR. That GMR percentage is not your ownership share. Reconcile the work identities, writer accounts and split documentation with the current representatives; do not add the two MLC percentages together as a settled split or assume a duplicate should be merged without review.
